title: Async stream handshake and tool-call backpressure certification for version-pinned onboarded models
creator: Priya Kaur
description: Goal: Certify that newly onboarded models (including those pinned to a specific version) correctly support asynchronous streaming handshakes and function/tool-calling semantics under backpressure and degraded conditions, and publish updated performance profiles for the model catalog. This ticket covers the verification harness, test cases, and publishing steps required before marking a model as 'streaming+toolcall certified' in the catalog. Scope excludes model architecture changes and focuses on serving/runtime integration and observable metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake conformance: model accepts initial streaming handshake with expected headers and echo behavior for at least 3 client SDK variants (python, node, go)
Backpressure handling: system demonstrates bounded memory and predictable latencies under 10x synthetic burst traffic with tool-calls enabled
Function/tool call fidelity: callbacks and tool metadata are delivered in-order and intact for both immediate and deferred (async) tool responses
Version pinning compatibility: pinned model variant (e.g., v2025-02-08) behaves identically to latest for streaming/tool-call semantics or differences are documented in the performance profile
Performance profile published: latency P50/P90/P99, token/sec throughput, and memory footprint recorded and attached to the model entry in the catalog
Observability hooks: tracing, request ids, and error-class tags present for all failing scenarios and surfaced in Console
test_plan: Create harness permutations: (1) short-seq low-concurrency, (2) long-seq medium-concurrency, (3) burst high-concurrency with KV-cache warm/cold
Simulate tool-calls: synchronous success, synchronous error, async deferred response (callback after delay), and tool timeouts
Inject backpressure: use proxy that throttles network reads/writes to emulate slow tool endpoints and limited GPU throughput
Run A/B between pinned and unpinned variants for the same model to capture divergence metrics
Automate smoke and regression tests in CI that run on every onboarding PR and gate certification checklist
Record telemetry: token latency histograms, per-request memory, dropped frames, and tool-call retransmits
rollout_plan: Phase 1: run harness in staging with canary traffic 1% for 24h; collect traces and compare against baseline
Phase 2: expand to 10% traffic in dedicated capacity for 48h; validate backpressure metrics under load
Phase 3: mark model as certified and publish performance profile to catalog; notify SDK teams to update docs
Rollback: revert to previous model variant and disable tool-calls routing if regression > 15% P90 latency increase or error rate > 1%
risks: Model encoding differences cause subtle ordering changes in streaming chunks that break some legacy SDKs
Backpressure in external tool endpoints results in unbounded queuing if not correctly signaled by runtime
Pinned variants expose quantization/kernel selection regressions not apparent in head model
Telemetry gaps under high load could mask regressions leading to false-positive certification
